hero.subtitle: From Linux servers to payment gateways, from React interfaces to blockchain smart contracts — we build, deploy, and stand behind complete solutions.

services.subtitle: We build. We deploy. We support.

items.title: Linux servers & DevOps
items.desc: Enterprise infrastructure, CI/CD, failover, security hardening, scaling

detail.summary: We stand up production Linux infrastructure and keep it running. That means Hetzner Cloud provisioning, hardened configurations, CI/CD pipelines, active-passive failover and the monitoring needed to catch problems before customers notice.
whatItIncludes: Ubuntu / Debian server provisioning with SSH-key-only access, nftables firewall rules, fail2ban and unattended security updates.
CI/CD pipelines through GitHub Actions — build, test, deploy, rollback — triggered on merge without manual SSH.
Systemd services, process supervision, zero-downtime reloads and structured logging to journald.
Active-passive failover with Cloudflare DNS switching, PostgreSQL streaming replication and tested failover drills.
Edge configuration on Cloudflare: TLS termination, WAF rules, rate limits, caching headers and origin certificates.
Monitoring through Prometheus and Grafana with alert routing — disk, memory, CPU, response latency, certificate expiry.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when your application is moving off a single hobby VPS into something that needs to survive a reboot, a traffic spike or a provider outage. Also when a compliance review asks for audit trails, patching policy and documented incident response.
detail.howWeWork: We start with a capacity plan: expected load, retention targets and the downtime budget you can tolerate. From there we build the stack in infrastructure-as-code, run through failover scenarios on staging, and hand over runbooks written in plain language.
detail.outcome: A production environment you can actually sleep next to, with known-good rollbacks, tested failover and dashboards that tell the truth about what is happening.

items.title: Backend & APIs
items.desc: Node.js/Express, RESTful & GraphQL APIs, third-party integrations

detail.summary: We design and build the Node.js backends that power web and mobile products — REST or GraphQL, authenticated, rate-limited and documented. The APIs we ship integrate cleanly with third parties and survive real traffic.
whatItIncludes: REST or GraphQL services in Node.js / Express, with request validation, structured errors and OpenAPI or schema-first documentation.
Third-party integrations (Stripe, PayPal, Twilio, shipping providers, partner APIs) with signed webhook handling and idempotent retries.
Background workers, queues and scheduled jobs for email, PDF generation, reconciliation and heavy processing.
Authentication and authorization: sessions, JWTs, OAuth flows and role-based access control.
Rate limiting, request tracing and observability hooks so you can see which endpoints are slow and why.
Test suites — unit, integration, contract — wired into CI so regressions get caught before production.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when a spreadsheet or a manual process is no longer enough, when the mobile team needs a real API, or when an existing backend has grown brittle and is blocking the product. It is also the right time when you are onboarding a second consumer (mobile, partner, internal tool) and need stable contracts.
detail.howWeWork: We start with the data model and the endpoint contract, not the framework. Once the contract is agreed we implement in thin vertical slices so you see working endpoints each week. Nothing goes to production without logging, searchable errors and a runbook for the integrations it touches.
detail.outcome: A backend your product team can build against with confidence, with documented endpoints, sensible limits and logs that answer the question 'what happened?' in minutes rather than hours.

items.title: Database architecture
items.desc: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB — design, replication, optimization

detail.summary: We design the database schemas and the operational setup behind them — PostgreSQL, MongoDB or MariaDB — so queries stay fast as data grows and backups actually restore. The goal is a database that is boring in the best way.
whatItIncludes: Schema design with proper normalization, indexes, foreign keys and migration history managed through Prisma, TypeORM or plain SQL migrations.
Replication setups: PostgreSQL streaming replicas, MongoDB replica sets, MariaDB primary-replica, with documented failover procedure.
Backup strategy: automated dumps, point-in-time recovery, offsite storage and scheduled restore drills that prove backups work.
Query optimization: explain plans, missing-index reviews, pagination fixes, N+1 audits on the application side.
Connection pooling with PgBouncer or equivalent, and pool sizing tuned against realistic load.
Role separation: migration user, application user, read-only reporting user — no more shared superuser passwords.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when queries have started to feel slow under normal load, when a migration looks risky, or when backups exist but nobody is sure they can be restored. Also when you are moving from a single-instance database toward replication for redundancy or reporting.
detail.howWeWork: We read the existing schema and query log first; optimization without data is guesswork. Then we propose the changes in writing, apply them to staging with representative data, and only promote to production after load tests and a restore drill.
detail.outcome: A database that answers queries in predictable time, survives a host failure, and whose backups have been restored at least once outside of an emergency.

items.title: React apps, corporate & personal websites
items.desc: SPAs, PWAs, corporate and personal sites, multi-language, SEO-optimized, mobile-first.

detail.summary: We build the React applications and websites businesses actually use — single-page apps, progressive web apps, corporate sites, personal portfolios, product pages. Written in modern React, multi-language, SEO-aware, and still readable on a five-year-old Android over 4G.
whatItIncludes: React 18 / 19 with Vite or Next.js — SPAs, PWAs or server-rendered pages — component structure designed for reuse across product lines.
Multi-language content through i18next, with hreflang tags, localized URLs and proper canonical handling for English, Bulgarian, Spanish or other languages.
SEO fundamentals: semantic HTML, structured data (JSON-LD), sitemaps, llms.txt for AI agents and meta tags the marketing team can actually read.
Responsive, mobile-first design reviewed on real device sizes — small Android screens and mid-range phones — not just desktop retina.
Progressive Web App setup when offline use or installability matters: service worker, manifest, caching strategy.
Accessibility basics: keyboard navigation, focus states, semantic HTML and colour contrast verified on real content.
Performance budget: core web vitals reviewed on real devices, image optimization, lazy loading and font subsetting.
Contact forms with spam mitigation, privacy-respecting analytics and an SSL setup that does not require a yearly panic.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when a v1 built on WordPress or a template is holding the product back, when the design team is delivering work off-the-shelf themes cannot render, when you are launching a new venture and the domain is the first thing a customer or investor will check, or when the current site loads in 12 seconds and you have noticed people bouncing.
detail.howWeWork: We start from the story the site needs to tell, the designs and the data — building in visible slices so the user-facing flow works end-to-end early. Reviews happen on a staging URL on real devices, not Figma comments. Every release ships with a bundle-size budget, a performance check on mid-range phones and a handover the marketing team can actually use.
detail.outcome: A frontend or website that loads quickly on a mid-range phone over 4G, reads well in every language it targets, ranks for the terms the business cares about, and that future developers can extend without rewriting half of it.

items.title: Payment integrations
items.desc: Stripe and PayPal integrations for web and mobile products

detail.summary: We connect products to Stripe Connect and PayPal Partner Commerce. The common thread: merchants receive funds directly, not through a platform-held balance.
whatItIncludes: Stripe Connect marketplaces with onboarding, split payments, application fees and payout management.
PayPal Partner Commerce (PPCP) with merchant onboarding, order capture and refund flows.
Signed webhook delivery with replay protection, idempotency keys and retry logic so missed events do not become lost payments.
Invoice generation, pay-by-link flows and recurring subscriptions where the payment rail supports them.
Reconciliation tools: transaction history, exportable reports, disputed-payment workflows and tax-ready statements.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when your product needs to take money from customers and split it between multiple parties, or when an existing payment setup is creating reconciliation problems.
detail.howWeWork: We map the money flow first — who pays, who receives, who takes a fee, what happens on a refund or a chargeback. Only then do we pick providers. Integrations go through a sandbox test matrix before a single real card or wallet is involved.
detail.outcome: A payment flow where merchants receive funds directly to their own account or wallet, the platform fee settles atomically, and the operations team has the reports and webhooks they need to close the books every month.

items.title: Web3 & blockchain
items.desc: EVM smart contracts, Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, DApp development

detail.summary: We write and ship smart contracts for client projects on EVM chains. Every contract is source-verified, audited with Slither and Mythril, and tested against the economic edge cases, not just the happy path. We build these for clients — we do not operate them.
whatItIncludes: Solidity 0.8.x contracts using OpenZeppelin v5 building blocks: Ownable, ReentrancyGuard, SafeERC20, AccessControl.
Test suite in Hardhat with fork tests against mainnet state where relevant, and gas-usage reports on every merge.
Static analysis with Slither and Mythril wired into CI; findings either fixed or documented with reasoning.
DApp integration using ethers.js, wagmi and viem, with wallet connection flows that work across MetaMask, WalletConnect and mobile wallets.
Deployment scripts with source verification on the target network's block explorer, plus a post-deploy smoke test.
Custom ERC-20 / 721 / 721A / 1155 token contracts where the client's project calls for them.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when your project requires on-chain logic that a database cannot enforce. It is the wrong tool when a Postgres transaction would do the job fine.
detail.howWeWork: We draft the threat model and the economic scenarios before any Solidity is written. Contracts are deployed first to Sepolia and exercised end-to-end, and only after static analysis is clean do we consider mainnet.
detail.outcome: Verified on-chain code that does what it says, whose source is public, whose test suite reproduces every claimed behaviour, and whose deployment is a single signed transaction — not a chain of upgrades.

items.title: Smart contract audit
items.desc: Security review, vulnerability detection, remediation reports

detail.summary: We review Solidity code the way it should be reviewed — by reading every line, running automated analysis and actually running the contracts against adversarial tests. The output is a written report with severity-ranked findings and concrete fix suggestions.
whatItIncludes: Line-by-line manual review focused on access control, arithmetic, external-call ordering, signature replay and upgrade paths.
Automated static analysis with Slither, Mythril, Aderyn and custom detectors, triaging every finding rather than listing raw output.
Fuzz and invariant testing with Foundry where the contract logic supports it — balances never go negative, total supply is preserved, no unauthorized mint path.
Gas review: unnecessary storage writes, expensive patterns, missing short-circuit checks.
A written report with executive summary, per-finding writeup (severity, impact, location, recommendation) and retest confirmation after fixes land.
A follow-up session to walk the team through the findings and the reasoning behind severity calls.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this before any contract holds real value on mainnet, before a governance vote migrates assets, or after a material change to code that a previous audit covered. It is also the right move when an exchange or launchpad requires an independent review.
detail.howWeWork: We start from the spec and the threat model, not the code. If either is missing we write them first — an audit that skips the spec is worth less than the PDF it is printed on. Fixes are reviewed in a second pass, and the final report states what was retested.
detail.outcome: A signed report you can share with stakeholders and counterparties, a test suite in better shape than when we started, and contracts whose remaining risks are known, named and accepted on purpose.

items.title: Monitoring systems
items.desc: Real-time dashboards for servers & industrial infrastructure

detail.summary: We build the dashboards and alerting that tell operators — digital or industrial — what is happening in real time. That includes servers, queues and, on the industrial side, sensors, PLCs and line equipment.
whatItIncludes: Metric pipelines: Prometheus or compatible collector, long-term storage, retention tuned to the questions operators actually ask.
Grafana dashboards grouped by audience — executive overview, oncall view, deep diagnostic — so nobody has to scroll through 40 panels to find the one they need.
Alert rules with useful thresholds, deduplication and routing to the right on-call rotation through PagerDuty, Slack or SMS.
Industrial integrations: OPC UA, Modbus and MQTT collectors for PLCs, historian writes and side-by-side display of IT and OT metrics.
Status pages, both internal and customer-facing, generated from the same source of truth as the alerts.
Post-incident review tools: timelines, metric snapshots and export so the team can actually learn from outages.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when outages are first noticed by customers rather than the team, when on-call engineers are drowning in noise, or when an industrial operation relies on people watching HMIs instead of alerts finding them. Also when a regulator or insurer wants evidence of operational oversight.
detail.howWeWork: We start by asking what question each dashboard is supposed to answer and who reads it. Alerts are calibrated against real historical data, not guesses, and every alert is required to have a runbook attached before it ships.
detail.outcome: A monitoring setup where every green screen means something, every alert means action is needed, and post-incident reviews have the data they need without scraping terminal history.

items.title: Admin panels
items.desc: Custom control panels, role-based access, workflow automation

detail.summary: We build the internal tools operations teams actually use — user management, content moderation, financial reconciliation, workflow automation. Custom-built to fit the process, not bent around an off-the-shelf CRM.
whatItIncludes: Role-based access control with audit logs: who changed what, when, and why — required for any operation that touches money or personal data.
Workflow automation: approval chains, state machines, bulk actions and scheduled tasks that used to be manual SQL.
Search and filtering that works on production data sizes, not just demo datasets.
Export tools: CSV, Excel, PDF, signed links, with date ranges and filters preserved for reproducibility.
Integration hooks into the systems the operations team already uses — email, Slack, ticketing and accounting exports.
Mobile-friendly layouts for the parts of the panel that are used away from a desk (approvals, quick lookups, status checks).
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when operations is running on a pile of read-only database queries and manual SQL updates, when customer support is asking for features that no public SaaS will cover, or when an external admin tool is charging per seat for functionality you already have the data for. It is also the right call when compliance asks for audit trails that the current stack cannot produce.
detail.howWeWork: We shadow the team doing the work first — what they actually click, what they copy-paste, where the friction is. The panel is built against those real tasks, not a feature list. We release incrementally so each new section replaces a real manual step.
detail.outcome: An internal tool that turns the operations team's painful manual routine into a short list of deliberate actions, with an audit trail that passes review and a velocity that does not tank when the team grows.

items.title: Access control
items.desc: Check-in/check-out, workforce tracking, attendance visibility

detail.summary: We deploy workforce access systems that replace paper sign-in sheets and spreadsheet timesheets — digital check-in / check-out, attendance tracking and the reporting layer on top. Built for real sites, including industrial ones where gloves and dust are part of the environment.
whatItIncludes: Digital check-in / check-out using RFID cards, phones or biometric readers, with offline queueing for when the network is down.
Shift scheduling, overtime calculation and attendance rules configured per site and role.
Visitor management: pre-registration, on-site badge printing, host notification and automatic badge expiry.
Reporting: who was on site when, for how long, filtered by site, team, role or date range — exportable for payroll and audits.
Integration with existing HR and payroll systems through API, CSV export or direct database bridge.
Alerting on tailgating, unauthorized access and missed check-outs, routed to the right supervisor.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when a paper system or Excel-based tracking is breaking down — either because of the number of people on site, compliance requirements, or a recent incident that made accountability matter. Also when you are preparing for an audit and cannot reconstruct who was on site last month.
detail.howWeWork: We walk the site before recommending hardware — a reader that lives in direct sun or a dusty corridor is not the same as one behind a reception desk. Rollout happens one zone at a time, with the paper system as a fallback until the digital one proves itself.
detail.outcome: A clear, queryable record of every site entry and exit, a payroll export that matches the timesheets, and supervisors who are alerted to exceptions instead of discovering them weeks later.

items.title: Video surveillance
items.desc: CCTV, alarm notifications, security company integration, recording

detail.summary: We design and deploy CCTV systems — cameras, recording, storage and the alerting that makes them actually useful. Configured to integrate with Bulgarian SOT services and responsive to the events that matter, not every leaf blowing past a lens.
whatItIncludes: Camera selection and placement based on field-of-view, lighting and purpose (identification, deterrence, overview).
NVR / DVR installation with appropriate storage retention — 7, 30 or 90 days depending on regulation and incident-review needs.
Motion and zone-based event alerts with push notifications, avoiding the usual storm of false positives from wind and shadows.
Integration with Bulgarian SOT (signal-response) providers so alarm events reach a monitored dispatch, not just a phone screen.
Remote viewing through web and mobile, with user roles so contractors and managers see different scopes.
Periodic health checks: disk usage, offline cameras, failed recordings — surfaced before a missing clip becomes a missed event.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when an existing system records but never triggers, when insurance requires documented coverage of specific areas, or when a new site needs a baseline surveillance setup without a three-letter integrator and a six-figure quote.
detail.howWeWork: We site-survey first, including a night visit under real lighting. Cameras are specified for their job, and the NVR is sized against retention, not marketing brochures. The system is handed over with written instructions the on-site team can actually follow.
detail.outcome: A surveillance setup that records reliably, alerts on events worth a response, and integrates with the security provider already on contract — so when something happens, the footage and the response are both there.

items.title: MVP development
items.desc: From idea to working product — validate, iterate, scale

detail.summary: We take an idea from a rough sketch to a working product you can put in front of real users — with the pragmatism to cut scope and the engineering standards not to ship something that falls over in the first week. Done honestly, an MVP teaches you what to build next.
whatItIncludes: Scope negotiation: separating the one or two hypotheses the MVP must test from everything else that can wait.
Technical architecture chosen for speed of iteration, not imagined Series A scale — a boring stack you can change later.
A working product end-to-end: signup, core flow, payment if relevant, admin view and analytics hooks.
Basic but real observability — logs, error tracking, a single dashboard — so the team can see what is happening in the first weeks.
A public deployment on real infrastructure, with domain, SSL, backups and a deployment pipeline that lets you ship fixes same-day.
A written handover: what was built, what was intentionally skipped and what the right next move is based on what was learned.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when you have an idea clear enough to describe in two paragraphs, a first set of potential users you can actually reach, and a budget measured in weeks rather than quarters. It is the wrong tool when the idea has no customer contact yet — paper and conversations are cheaper.
detail.howWeWork: We spend the first week narrowing scope, not coding — removing features is how an MVP stays an MVP. From there we build in weekly increments against a public staging URL, with a real user trying the flow by the end of week two.
detail.outcome: A product in real users' hands within weeks, data and feedback to guide the next round of work, and a codebase that a future team can either keep building on or honestly retire — decided on evidence, not hope.

gembapay.tagline: One API for card and PayPal payments — funds never sit with the platform.
gembapay.cardDescription: A payment gateway that unifies Stripe and PayPal behind a single checkout and API. Merchants keep 99% of every transaction, with automatic fee splits and payouts straight to their own accounts.
gembapay.heroIntro: GembaPay lets merchants price in 86+ currencies and accept card or PayPal payments through one API. Every payment routes directly from customer to merchant — the platform never holds funds. Merchants wake up to money already in their own account.

problem.title: The payments trilemma
problem.body: Merchants selling across borders usually end up juggling three or four separate gateways, each with its own dashboard, fee structure and settlement schedule. The result is fragmented accounting, slow settlement and a dependency on platforms that can freeze or reverse payments at any time.

solution.title: One gateway, two rails
solution.body: GembaPay sits in front of Stripe and PayPal as a single integration. Card and PayPal payments ride Stripe Connect and PayPal Partner rails with an automated split, so the merchant is paid directly into their own account and the platform never holds a balance.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaPay is
items: A payment router that connects customer cards directly to the merchant's own Stripe or PayPal account.
An automated 1%/99% split, so the merchant is paid directly and the platform never holds a balance.
A pricing engine that quotes 86+ currencies in real time and lets customers pay in the currency they already use.
A merchant dashboard with transaction history, invoice generation, webhooks and Stripe Connect or PayPal Partner onboarding in one place.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaPay is not
items: Not a holder of funds — we never take possession of merchant or customer money, not even briefly.
Not a crypto exchange — we don't convert currencies, we only route payments to the destination the merchant chose.
Not a dispute handler — Stripe and PayPal disputes are handled by Stripe and PayPal.
Not KYC-free for fiat rails — Stripe Connect and PayPal Partner require the same compliance you'd meet anywhere else.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Everything a merchant needs to accept card and PayPal payments, with reconciliation that actually adds up at the end of the month.

items.title: Unified checkout
items.desc: A single embedded flow offers crypto, cards and PayPal. Customers pick the method they use; merchants don't configure a different integration for each.

items.title: Direct settlement to the merchant
items.desc: Payments settle straight into the merchant's own Stripe or PayPal account. No sweeping, no batch settlement, no holding account.

items.title: Real-time multi-currency pricing
items.desc: Invoice amounts are quoted in the merchant's display currency and converted at the moment of payment.

items.title: Stripe Connect + PayPal Partner
items.desc: Certified integrations that handle onboarding, split settlement and payouts, so merchants keep their existing card acceptance.

items.title: WooCommerce plugin
items.desc: A drop-in WordPress plugin adds GembaPay as a checkout option in minutes, with configurable chains and currency display.

items.title: Webhooks and invoices
items.desc: Every confirmed payment triggers a signed webhook; invoices can be generated with a customer email, amount and expiry for pay-by-link use.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaPay is split into layers that never share custody of funds. The API layer, written in Node.js and Express on PostgreSQL with Prisma, stores invoices, merchants and transaction history but never holds balances. The React frontend is a stateless client that reads the merchant dashboard and guides customers through payment.

Every transaction path is settlement-in-one-step. A card payment goes through Stripe Connect, where Stripe handles the destination transfer and the application fee; PayPal follows the same logical shape through Partner Commerce. The platform records the invoice and the outcome, and nothing else.

The resulting system has no platform balance to drain. A full compromise of the GembaPay servers cannot move merchant funds, because Stripe and PayPal settle directly into the merchant's own connected account.

items.title: E-commerce stores
items.desc: WooCommerce and custom storefronts accept card and PayPal payments through one integration, without building a separate payments stack.

items.title: SaaS subscriptions
items.desc: Monthly subscription links issued through the API, with recurring card billing via Stripe and one-off crypto renewals.

items.title: Freelancers and agencies
items.desc: International invoices sent in the client's currency, settled to the merchant's own account in one click.

items.title: Donations and memberships
items.desc: Non-profits and creator platforms accept multi-currency donations routed straight to their own account, with no platform skim beyond the 1% fee.

security.title: Security
security.body: Security is a property of the architecture, not a checklist added at the end. The guiding principle is that GembaPay should fail safely: if the platform goes down, in-flight payments are either confirmed by the provider or they simply never happened, and no merchant balance is at risk either way.

items.label: No platform-held balance
items.value: The platform never takes possession of merchant or customer funds. Smart contracts enforce the 1%/99% split atomically.

items.label: Audit posture
items.value: Static analysis runs in CI on every merge, with findings either fixed or documented before release.

items.label: Access control
items.value: OpenZeppelin Ownable governs admin functions (fee recipient, paused state); ReentrancyGuard protects all value transfers.

items.label: No upgradeability
items.value: Merchant funds settle directly into the merchant's own Stripe or PayPal account. The platform has no balance to freeze, lose or misapply.

items.label: Operational monitoring
items.value: Signed webhooks, request logging and Stripe/PayPal dispute handling give merchants the same visibility they'd have with a traditional gateway.

gembaticket.cardDescription: GembaTicket is a completely free, next-generation online ticketing platform built on web3, blockchain and smart-contract technology, that lets organizers sell tickets online and receive the proceeds in their own balances the moment a purchase is made.
gembaticket.heroIntro: GembaTicket is a completely free, next-generation online ticketing platform built on web3, blockchain and smart-contract technology, that lets organizers sell tickets online and receive the proceeds in their own balances the moment a purchase is made — removing the need for printed paper tickets and box-office queues, giving full control over access to the event's different entrances, and leaving a permanent NFT keepsake in the hands of attendees.

problem.title: Ticketing built on held funds and friction
problem.body: Traditional ticketing platforms hold the buyer's money for weeks and release it long after the event, taking 10-15% along the way. GembaTicket settles to the organizer directly and holds nothing.

solution.title: Payment in, ticket out, nothing held in between
solution.body: GembaTicket sells every ticket through GembaPay — card or PayPal, the organizer's choice. The ticket itself is a database record protected by an HMAC-signed QR code that rotates every 30 seconds and is sent to the buyer's email address. End users access their tickets without needing to create an account on the platform.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Designed so organizers run events the way they always did — and Web3 shows up only when someone actively asks for it.

items.title: Dual ticket modes
items.desc: Tickets work like any standard system — email delivery, rotating QR code, no account required.

items.title: QR rotation
items.desc: Ticket QR codes are HMAC-signed with a TTL and valid for 30 seconds. A shared screenshot stops validating the moment the 30-second timer rolls over.

items.title: GembaPay-powered checkout
items.desc: Buyers pay in EUR, USD and 51 more fiat currencies. Funds route directly to the organizer's Stripe or PayPal account, with no platform-held balance.

items.title: Multi-organizer marketplace
items.desc: A single platform hosts multiple organizers, each with their own events, branding and payout rails. Revenue splits are configured per event.

items.title: Clone-factory contracts
items.desc: Each event deploys a minimal EIP-1167 clone of the ticket template on GembaBlockchain, giving every end user access to take a keepsake of the event.

items.title: Scanner app
items.desc: Door staff use a phone, tablet or any internet-connected scanning device that validates QR codes in real time.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaTicket splits into three cleanly separated layers. The payments layer is GembaPay, which handles fiat and crypto checkout and settles funds directly to the organizer. The ticketing layer is a Node.js and Express API on PostgreSQL and Redis that stores events, ticket records and rotating QR secrets — it never holds customer funds or private keys.

Organizers can set up different ticket price tiers (Early Bird, Regular, VIP, Stage — max 10) and timers for when a tier becomes active — by date, when the previous tier sells out, or a combination of both. Different access zones can be set per ticket tier, so attendees enter through different gates.

At the door, scanning is entirely Web2. The scanner app sends a signed QR payload and a timestamp to the API; the API validates the signature, checks the ticket is active and returns pass (green) or fail (red) in under 200 ms. Organizers have full control over access to their event — they can have different scanning devices per zone, each scanner knowing exactly which ticket tier to admit and which not. For example: the Regular scanner admits all zones, the VIP scanner only VIP and Stage, the Stage scanner only Stage. Scanners can also be configured for multi-day festivals and conferences — it's all in the organizer's hands.

The organizer has an intuitive interface to manage everything: see stats for sold/remaining tickets and collected revenue, add new tiers or increase the supply of existing ones, and watch in real time how many attendees have passed through the entrance scanners.

Anyone can register as an organizer completely free of charge. The only requirement to start creating events and accepting direct payments to their own balances is to register with the payment provider GembaPay — from there they get an API key and webhook secret, which they add to their account, and the "Create event" button becomes active.

items.title: Concerts and festivals
items.desc: Music events with ticket tiers or without, session tracks, and optional VIP NFT collectibles for attendees who want a lasting keepsake.

items.title: Sports, venues and conferences
items.desc: Recurring events that benefit from rotating QR codes against screenshot fraud and from direct settlement to the organizer's own account.

items.title: Clubs and small parties
items.desc: Organizers who want a pay-link workflow with multi-currency acceptance and minimal fees compared to mainstream platforms.

items.title: Token-gated events
items.desc: Events with tiered access, where entry rights differ by ticket type and gate.

security.title: Security
security.body: Two categories of risk: funds and tickets. We address funds by never holding them — GembaPay settles every purchase directly to the organizer. No administrative or other hidden fees are charged, no unwanted insurance is added — the customer pays the price they see, and the organizer has access to up to 99% of that amount within seconds! We address tickets by having users receive their ticket seconds after purchase, straight to their pre-verified email — with no risk of loss or an undelivered courier package — and by tying ticket validity to QR codes that rotate, so leaked screenshots lose value within seconds. Tickets are not tied to a name, and you can always gift or resell the ticket you bought.

items.label: No funds held by the platform
items.value: No private keys stored for users, no escrow balance held on the platform. Funds route through GembaPay straight to the organizer.

items.label: QR rotation
items.value: Ticket QR codes are HMAC-signed with a short TTL. A shared screenshot stops validating as soon as the timer rolls.

items.label: Audit posture
items.value: Slither and Mythril audits completed on v2 contracts; no critical findings. All contracts use OpenZeppelin v5 primitives.

items.label: Clone-factory pattern
items.value: EIP-1167 minimal proxies keep the cost of deploying an event at =0 thanks to GembaBlockchain. Organizers and end users never know about it, yet can always inspect the smart-contract code.

educhain.tagline: A safe Web3 sandbox where teachers learn before students do.
educhain.cardDescription: An EU-focused educational platform with role-based access, live leaderboards, an NFT gallery and a structured 16-hour student curriculum plus a 3-day teacher training program.
educhain.heroIntro: EduChain prepares European classrooms for Web3 without putting anyone at financial risk. Everything runs on GembaBlockchain testnet, so students can deploy tokens, mint NFTs and trade safely while teachers manage the whitelist. A dedicated training track certifies educators before they step into the classroom.

problem.title: Web3 curriculum without a safe playground
problem.body: Schools that want to teach blockchain run into two walls. Mainnet is too risky — students can't experiment with real assets, and regulators won't allow minors to touch them anyway. Existing sandboxes are either too abstract, with no real wallets or real deploys, or too technical — Hardhat CLI, testnet faucets and MetaMask for eleven-year-olds — and neither form teaches teachers anything at all.

solution.title: A guided GembaBlockchain testnet classroom
solution.body: EduChain is a full-stack learning environment running on GembaBlockchain testnet, where every student has a real wallet, real gas and real transactions — just without real financial consequences. A teacher-administered whitelist gates access, a built-in faucet funds exercises, and the curriculum walks teachers through a 3-day training program before students touch anything. Structured lessons, live leaderboards and an NFT gallery give educators the instructional scaffolding that general-purpose testnets lack.

whatWeAre.title: What EduChain is
items: A classroom-grade Web3 sandbox running end-to-end on GembaBlockchain testnet, including ERC20 token deployment, ERC721 NFTs and a peer-to-peer marketplace.
A role-based platform with distinct dashboards for students, teachers and administrators, including whitelist management and progress tracking.
A 16-hour structured student curriculum paired with a 3-day teacher training track that certifies educators before they lead students.
A GDPR-aware product designed for European schools, with data minimization and a pedagogical flow reviewed against EU classroom norms.

whatWeAreNot.title: What EduChain is not
items: Not a mainnet platform — nothing students do has financial value, and that is the point.
Not an investment simulator or trading game — the goal is understanding the mechanics, not speculating.
Not a replacement for a teacher — materials guide, but a trained educator runs the session.
Not a general-purpose developer tool — the UX is tuned for a 14-year-old, not for a Solidity engineer.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Everything a classroom needs to move through a Web3 unit in one semester, with enough structure that a teacher without a CS background can still lead confidently.

items.title: Role-based dashboards
items.desc: Students, teachers and administrators each get a tailored view with the tools and data appropriate to their role.

items.title: Built-in GMB faucet
items.desc: Teachers fund student wallets with GembaBlockchain testnet GMB from a shared pool — no external faucet queues, no lesson interrupted by empty gas tanks.

items.title: ERC20 and NFT workshops
items.desc: Structured exercises that walk students through deploying a token, minting an NFT collection and listing items on a marketplace.

items.title: Live leaderboards
items.desc: Classroom-wide scoreboards reward task completion and quiz performance — useful for gamified units without adding real-money incentives.

items.title: Teacher training track
items.desc: A 3-day program certifies teachers in the platform's pedagogy, the underlying Web3 concepts and classroom-management specifics.

items.title: Moralis + Pinata
items.desc: NFT metadata and images store on IPFS through Pinata; Moralis indexes student activity across the testnet for dashboards and analytics.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The platform runs on six GembaBlockchain testnet contracts written in Solidity 0.8.19 with OpenZeppelin primitives: a Whitelist, a GameToken ERC20, two NFT contracts (one predefined, one custom), a TokenMarketplace and an ETHFaucet. Every contract is a real, deployed artifact on a real network, so students see transaction hashes, gas fees and block confirmations exactly as they would on mainnet.

The frontend is React 18 with ethers.js v5, designed to be usable without previous blockchain exposure. Wallet onboarding is guided step by step, and most classroom actions are wrapped in UI that explains what's happening on-chain in plain language before sending the transaction.

Teachers administer the environment through a dedicated dashboard that controls whitelist entries, faucet allocations, curriculum progress and student reports. EduChain deliberately doesn't integrate with student identity systems or gradebooks — the school retains that data under its own policies, and EduChain only tracks what it needs to teach.

items.title: Secondary schools
items.desc: A semester-long technology unit that gives 14–18-year-olds practical exposure to blockchain mechanics in a controlled environment.

items.title: Vocational and technical colleges
items.desc: Foundation-level Web3 training for students moving toward fintech, software and emerging-tech careers.

items.title: Teacher professional development
items.desc: Continuing-education programs for educators who need to teach blockchain but haven't worked with it themselves.

items.title: EU-funded pilots
items.desc: Research projects on digital literacy and emerging technology in classrooms that need a GDPR-aware sandbox to demo in.

permitiv.tagline: Unify shift planning, check-in, permits and inventory for industrial teams.
permitiv.cardDescription: A modular SaaS platform for refineries, plants and workforce-heavy operations. Swap fragmented spreadsheets and standalone tools for one system, with an optional self-hosted Docker edition.
permitiv.heroIntro: Permitiv — the platform at the foundation of project Atlas — brings shift planning, digital check-in and check-out, inventory, digital permits, an integrated office suite and an AI assistant into one platform built for industrial work. Designed alongside refinery operators, it replaces the usual patchwork of spreadsheets and vendor tools with something teams can actually run end-to-end.

problem.title: Industrial operations stitched together by spreadsheets
problem.body: Walk into a refinery turnaround, a large construction site or a busy plant and you'll see the same thing — shift rosters on a whiteboard, permits on paper, inventory in Excel, check-in on a clipboard. Each vendor tool covers one slice and none of them talk to each other. The people who actually run the work spend more time reconciling spreadsheets than planning the work itself.

solution.title: One modular platform
solution.body: Permitiv puts shift planning, check-in and check-out, inventory, digital permits, an integrated office suite and an AI assistant under one roof. Modules activate independently, so an operator can start with scheduling and check-in and add permits, inventory and documents as the team is ready. For clients with strict data-residency requirements, the entire platform runs as a self-hosted Docker deployment on their own infrastructure.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Designed alongside refinery and plant operators — not in a design studio in a different city — so each module solves a problem somebody has actually been paid to solve.

items.title: Shift planning
items.desc: Rosters with skills, certifications and rest rules. Changes propagate instantly to crew members on mobile.

items.title: Check-in and check-out
items.desc: Badge, QR or biometric entry with timestamps, location and shift context. Attendance rolls up to payroll and access control.

items.title: Digital permits
items.desc: Permit-to-work, hot-work and confined-space permits issued, reviewed and archived on the platform with full audit trail.

items.title: Inventory and parts
items.desc: Tool and consumable tracking, low-stock alerts and issue/return workflows tied to work orders.

items.title: Integrated office
items.desc: Documents, tasks and messaging inside the same platform, so day-to-day coordination doesn't need a separate SaaS stack.

items.title: AI assistant
items.desc: A contextual assistant that answers procedural questions, drafts reports and finds information across the platform's own data.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Permitiv is a classic modular monolith — React on the frontend, Node.js and PostgreSQL on the backend — packaged so that every module is independently deployable. A client who only needs shift planning and check-in runs a slim subset; a refinery that wants permits, inventory, documents and the AI assistant turns the rest on without migrating data.

Deployment comes in two shapes. The hosted SaaS runs on GEMBA's Hetzner infrastructure with failover and database replication, which is the fastest way for most teams to start. The self-hosted Docker edition bundles the same stack into containers that run on the client's own servers — useful for sites with strict data-residency, offline or security requirements.

The AI assistant is layered on top rather than baked in. It reads what the platform already knows — shift logs, permit history, inventory movements, documents — and answers in context. It doesn't retrain on client data, and it doesn't leave the boundary of the client's installation when self-hosted.

items.title: Refineries and chemical plants
items.desc: Turnaround planning, crew logistics and permit management during high-intensity shutdown and commissioning windows.

items.title: Construction and industrial services
items.desc: Site attendance, tool tracking and document control across distributed crews and subcontractors.

items.title: Workforce-heavy operations
items.desc: Any business where shift-based crews, badges and permits matter more than conference-room software.

items.title: Regulated sites
items.desc: Facilities that require auditable permit history, attendance records and controlled access, with the option to host everything internally.

gembablockchain.tagline: A public testnet we built to earn trust in the web3 engineering community — not to raise money.
gembablockchain.cardDescription: A testnet-only, EVM-compatible Proof-of-Stake research chain built in-house to prove our engineering in public. There is no mainnet, no coin sale and no financial product — the test coin has no monetary value and exists only to make the testnet usable.
gembablockchain.heroIntro: GembaBlockchain is a fully transparent, decentralized, permissionless Proof-of-Stake Layer 1 built on Cosmos SDK + Cosmos EVM and CometBFT. Its native coin, Gemba (GMB), is a utility coin — staking, gas and access — not a speculative asset. Anyone with enough stake can validate; anyone can hold and send GMB. The founder holds no special power: reserves never vote and the founder never validates with privilege.

problem.title: Public infrastructure shouldn't depend on one operator
problem.body: Institutions that want to put services on-chain usually face a choice between permissioned chains run by a single vendor — who can decide who participates — and public chains whose economics are driven by speculation and unpredictable fees. Neither is a neutral, durable foundation for public-interest services. Validator sets are capped, governance concentrates, and the token's value detaches from its actual use.

solution.title: A neutral chain owned by its participants
solution.body: GembaBlockchain uses CometBFT Proof-of-Stake with permissionless validator entry and full EVM compatibility, so any Solidity or MetaMask workflow runs against it unchanged. It runs on testnet only: mainnet is not launched, the coin is not sold, not listed and has no monetary value. We built it as public proof of our engineering, not as a product to sell.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaBlockchain is
items: A permissionless PoS Layer 1 — bond GMB above the threshold and you validate; no KYC, no whitelist, no privileged validators.
Fully EVM-compatible — Solidity, 0x addresses, MetaMask, Foundry, ethers/viem and standard JSON-RPC all work out of the box.
Zero inflation by design — the test coin supply is fixed at genesis and never minted again.
A utility chain for institutions and organizations to deliver services — cheaper access, workplace access control, tickets and perks.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaBlockchain is not
items: Not built for speculation — the project seeds no liquidity, runs no exchange or DEX, and makes no public token sale.
Not operator-controlled — no central party can decide who participates or change the rules unilaterally.
Not inflationary — there is no minting after genesis and no dynamic-issuance lever.
Not a closed system — it is a public, sovereign chain anyone can build on and validate.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Everything a public-interest L1 needs: permissionless validation, EVM tooling, instant finality and a fixed, honest supply.

items.title: Permissionless validation
items.desc: Stake-only entry into a large active set (CometBFT). Power is bought with locked GMB, so no one can flood the validator set cheaply.

items.title: Full EVM compatibility
items.desc: Deploy Solidity contracts, connect MetaMask and use Foundry/Hardhat against the chain's JSON-RPC — chainId 821207.

items.title: Zero inflation
items.desc: Fixed 100M GMB; validator rewards stream from a pre-minted reserve and fees, never from new issuance.

items.title: Instant finality
items.desc: CometBFT BFT consensus gives fast, final blocks with no reorgs.

items.title: Self-hosted explorer
items.desc: GembaScan (Blockscout) provides a standard block-explorer API, contract verification and full transaction history.

items.title: On-chain governance
items.desc: Chain parameters via the Cosmos gov module; treasuries via a Solidity Governor + Timelock, with reserves excluded from voting.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaBlockchain is Cosmos EVM (an off-the-shelf, production-used permissionless PoS + EVM stack) plus a thin Gemba layer: two small Go modules — a zero-inflation validator-reward streamer that pays from a pre-minted reserve, and a fee-split that routes part of every fee back into a public reserve — together with the Solidity treasury, governance and application contracts.

Consensus is CometBFT BFT Proof-of-Stake: validators bond GMB, produce blocks with instant finality, and are slashed for objectively-provable faults (double-signing, downtime). The EVM execution layer makes the chain a drop-in target for the entire Ethereum toolchain, while the native coin and staking live in Cosmos modules.

Reserves (public/municipal, foundation, DAO, contingency, validator) are held in non-voting accounts and released only through governance + timelock — there is no admin key that can drain them and no privileged validator that outranks the rest.

items.title: Public institutions
items.desc: Municipalities and agencies delivering citizen services on a neutral chain they help run — under the same rules as everyone else.

items.title: Organizations & enterprises
items.desc: Companies integrating access control, tickets, perks and payments on a low-cost, EVM-compatible chain.

items.title: Validators
items.desc: Anyone with enough GMB to bond can join the active set permissionlessly and earn from fees and the reserve.

items.title: Developers
items.desc: Web3 builders deploying Solidity dApps with familiar tooling (MetaMask, Foundry, ethers) against a sovereign chain.

security.title: Security & decentralization
security.body: Decentralization is the goal the design binds to mechanisms, not promises: permissionless entry from block zero, no lever to re-close it, and an economic model where attacking the chain costs more than it secures.

items.label: BFT Proof-of-Stake
items.value: CometBFT needs >1/3 of bonded stake to halt and ≥2/3 to forge — and that stake is slashed. The target is cost-to-attack ≥ 3× value secured.

items.label: Fixed supply
items.value: 100M GMB minted once at genesis; 0% inflation. The mint module is disabled.

items.label: No privileged power
items.value: Reserves never vote, the founder never validates with privilege, and funds leave reserves only via governance + timelock.

items.label: Pre-v1 upstream
items.value: Cosmos EVM is pinned to a known-good version; custom modules are isolated, and a public launch waits on the upstream audit and our own review.

gembakitchen.tagline: AI-powered operations for professional kitchens — inventory, recipes, menu and food-cost, with an assistant you can talk to.
gembakitchen.cardDescription: A multi-tenant SaaS that runs a restaurant's back-of-house: live inventory, recipes with automatic food-cost, menu and sales, plus a built-in AI assistant you can chat with — or speak to in English or Bulgarian — to record sales, check stock or build recipes by voice. Ships with a 64-recipe professional cookbook teams can copy into their own kitchen. Billed through GembaPay with a 72-hour free trial.
gembakitchen.heroIntro: GembaKitchen is an AI kitchen-operations platform for restaurants, cafés and professional kitchens. Each business gets an isolated workspace where it manages products and stock, recipes and menu, sales and reports — and an assistant powered by Claude that reads its live data and acts on it through function-calling. Staff can type or talk to the kitchen in English or Bulgarian; it answers in natural voice, records a sale, flags low stock, or drafts a new recipe. A curated cookbook of professional recipes is one click away from any kitchen.

problem.title: Running a kitchen is spreadsheets, guesswork and shrinkage
problem.body: Most kitchens track stock on paper or in spreadsheets, never really know the food-cost of a dish, and discover shortages only when they run out mid-service. Recipe knowledge lives in one chef's head, sales aren't tied back to ingredient consumption, and nobody has time to keep it all current. The data exists — it's just scattered, stale and impossible to query in the middle of a busy shift.

solution.title: One workspace, plus an assistant that does the typing
solution.body: GembaKitchen keeps inventory, recipes, menu and sales in one place and links them: selling a dish automatically deducts its recipe's ingredients and books the revenue and cost. On top of that sits an AI assistant that can read every number and change it for you — by chat or by voice, in English or Bulgarian. Ask it what's low, tell it you sold ten cheeseburgers, or have it build a recipe and put it on the menu; it calls the right tools and confirms exactly what changed.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaKitchen is
items: A multi-tenant SaaS for professional and home kitchens — each restaurant's data lives in an isolated workspace.
A linked back-of-house: products, recipes, menu and sales that stay in sync, with automatic food-cost and profit per dish.
An AI assistant powered by Claude that reads your live kitchen data and acts on it through function-calling.
A voice interface in English and Bulgarian — talk to your kitchen, and it talks back in natural speech.
A professional cookbook of 64+ curated recipes any kitchen can copy in one click.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaKitchen is not
items: Not a generic POS — it's the back-of-house brain the POS never gives you.
Not another spreadsheet you have to update by hand; the assistant does the data entry.
Not a shared database — every kitchen is isolated in its own multi-tenant workspace.
Not locked to one language — the assistant reads, writes and speaks both English and Bulgarian.

features.title: Features
features.intro: Everything a kitchen needs to know its numbers — and an assistant to keep them current.

items.title: Talk to your kitchen
items.desc: Chat or speak to a Claude-powered assistant in English or Bulgarian; it records sales, checks stock and answers questions, then replies in natural voice.

items.title: Live inventory & alerts
items.desc: Track stock in real units with reorder levels; selling a dish deducts its ingredients automatically and flags anything that drops too low.

items.title: Recipes with food-cost
items.desc: Build a recipe once and watch the cost and margin of every dish update from your real ingredient prices.

items.title: Professional cookbook
items.desc: Browse a curated library of 64+ recipes across eight cuisines and copy any into your own kitchen — it never touches your kitchen until you add it.

items.title: Sales & reports
items.desc: Revenue, food-cost %, profit per dish, top sellers, low-stock and waste — charted over 7, 30 or 90 days.

items.title: AI builds it for you
items.desc: Ask the assistant to create products, recipes or menu items and it drafts them from culinary knowledge, then puts them on the menu.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaKitchen is a Node.js + Express + Prisma backend on a dedicated PostgreSQL database, with three React/Vite front-ends — a customer dashboard, a marketing site and an owner console — behind Apache and Cloudflare. Every tenant table carries a restaurant id, so one kitchen can never see another's data.

The assistant uses Claude (Anthropic) with tool-use: a tenant-scoped tool loop where the model can read inventory, recipes and menu and act — record a sale, log a purchase, or create a recipe — always limited to the caller's own kitchen. Voice is handled by ElevenLabs for natural text-to-speech and speech-to-text, so the same assistant works by typing or by talking in English and Bulgarian.
Billing runs through GembaPay: a 72-hour free trial opens at signup, then monthly plans are paid via a GembaPay payment request, with the subscription extended by a signed webhook.

items.title: Restaurants & cafés
items.desc: Keep stock, recipes and menu in sync, know the food-cost of every dish, and let staff record sales by voice during service.

items.title: Professional kitchens
items.desc: Standardise recipes across a team, copy proven recipes from the cookbook, and watch margins and waste in the reports.

items.title: Catering & cloud kitchens
items.desc: Run multiple menus from one isolated workspace and cost each dish from real ingredient prices.

items.title: Home cooks
items.desc: A simpler mode to manage a pantry, recipes and shopping — with the same assistant to talk to.

security.title: Security & privacy
security.body: GembaKitchen isolates every kitchen and stores only what it needs: business data, not card numbers.

items.label: Tenant isolation
items.value: Every record is scoped to a restaurant id in a dedicated database that is never shared with other apps.

items.label: No card data
items.value: Payments run through GembaPay; GembaKitchen never stores card numbers and verifies billing webhooks by HMAC signature.

items.label: Account security
items.value: Email-verified signup, JWT sessions and optional two-factor authentication (email code or authenticator app).

problem.title: Work needs a soundtrack — without the friction

whatWeAre.title: What GEMBA RECORDS Radio is

features.intro: Everything you need to put on good music and get back to work — nothing you don't.

architecture.title: How it's built
paragraphs: GEMBA RECORDS Radio is a lightweight React + Vite web app that plays three live stations over HLS (hls.js in the browser, native HLS on iOS) — chosen specifically because plain live MP3 streams stalled on mobile, while HLS plays robustly everywhere, including iPhone.

The same app is a PWA, so visitors can install it to a phone home screen or desktop directly from the browser, and it is packaged as an Android app (Capacitor) distributed both as a downloadable APK and, soon, on Google Play.

The audio is streamed from an AzuraCast station server and delivered behind an Apache reverse proxy with Cloudflare in front, so the player talks to gembarecords.com endpoints and the upstream source stays hidden.

items.title: Teams at work

gembapass.tagline: Access passes & membership cards — for workplaces, clubs and gyms, with the blockchain made invisible.
gembapass.cardDescription: A subscription SaaS that issues soulbound access-pass NFTs on GembaBlockchain — for workplace access or time-bound membership cards (clubs, gyms, season passes). Members get a normal account; the backend custodies wallets and signs invisibly. Remove someone, or let a membership expire, and their pass dies in one click. No wallets for users, no PII on-chain.
gembapass.heroIntro: GembaPass is the first dApp built on GembaBlockchain: a multi-tenant access-control SaaS where an organisation subscribes, adds users and issues passes in a few clicks — for workplace access or time-bound membership cards (clubs, gyms, season passes). Each pass is an anonymous, soulbound capability NFT — but nobody using the system ever sees a wallet, a seed phrase or gas. The contract is deliberately minimal; zones, hours, rights, validity and logs all live off-chain.

problem.title: Blockchain access control that no one can actually use
problem.body: On-chain credentials are tamper-evident and auditable, but real workplaces can't ask every employee to install a wallet, guard a seed phrase and pay gas. Meanwhile, putting identities and movement logs on an immutable ledger collides head-on with GDPR. So most 'blockchain access' projects either stay demos or quietly become databases with a logo.

solution.title: Managed keys by design, invisible by default
solution.body: GembaPass makes the chain invisible: the backend silently creates and encrypts a wallet per employee and signs every on-chain action through the platform issuer. Employees just get an email + password. Because GMB is not a financial instrument and no funds are ever held, custody carries no money-transmitter or licensing burden. Passes are soulbound; issuing is a mint, firing is an issuer-only force-burn — and PII never touches the chain.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaPass is
items: A multi-tenant SaaS that issues soulbound access-pass NFTs (one per employee) on GembaBlockchain.
A managed-key system that keeps the infrastructure invisible — staff use a normal email and password, never a key of their own.
A dumb on-chain contract plus a smart off-chain backend: zones, hours, rights, PINs and logs live in PostgreSQL, never on-chain.
Both a cloud multi-tenant product and an on-prem single-tenant deployment for organizations that want autonomy.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaPass is not
items: Not a wallet your employees have to manage — they never see keys, seeds or gas.
Not a place where personal data goes on-chain — identity, movement logs and PINs stay off-chain and GDPR-erasable.
Not a transferable token — passes are soulbound and can only be minted or force-burned by the issuer.
Not a financial product — no funds are held, so there is no exchange, custody-license or AML surface.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Everything an organization needs to hand out and revoke physical access — without anyone realizing they're using a blockchain.

items.title: One-click issue & revoke
items.desc: Granting a pass mints a soulbound NFT; firing someone force-burns it (issuer-only, no approval) so every door closes at once.

items.title: Invisible managed credentials
items.desc: The backend creates and AES-256-GCM-encrypts a wallet per employee and signs on their behalf; the access path never even decrypts it.

items.title: Offline-first door scanner
items.desc: A phone-based PWA reads the pass QR, verifies on-chain validity plus zone rights, hours and an optional PIN, and toggles entry/exit.

items.title: Zones, hours & PINs
items.desc: Define zones with access windows and mark sensitive ones PIN-protected — all enforced by the backend, not the contract.

items.title: Operator onboarding
items.desc: An operator panel onboards partner companies with an optional free grace period; companies can also self-register.

items.title: Subscription billing
items.desc: Monthly billing through GembaPay; lapsed subscriptions hit a grace period before access stops — never a silent burn.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaPass pairs a deliberately minimal ERC-1155 contract — GembaAccessPass, soulbound, issuer-only mint and force-burn, one token id per person — with a Node.js + Express + Prisma backend on PostgreSQL and Redis. The contract answers only 'is this credential alive?'; everything human (identity, zones, hours, rights, logs, PINs) lives off-chain, behind row-level tenant isolation.
Issuing a pass generates a branded QR, pins the image and metadata to IPFS, and records the credential against the employee's managed identity on the testnet chain. Staff never see or handle a key.

Five React frontends (landing, company dashboard, operator dashboard, employee app and scanner PWA) sit behind an Apache reverse proxy with Cloudflare TLS. The platform issuer wallet — the only privileged key — signs all mints and burns; employee keys are never needed for the access flow.

items.title: Companies & SMEs
items.desc: Issue, manage and revoke employee access passes from a single dashboard, with per-zone rights and access hours.

items.title: Public institutions
items.desc: Workplace and facility access on a public, auditable chain, with personal data kept off-chain for GDPR compliance.

items.title: Multi-site organizations
items.desc: Operators onboard many companies (cloud multi-tenant) or deploy a dedicated single-tenant instance on-prem.

items.title: Employees
items.desc: A simple app shows the access pass, lets them set a PIN, and — for the technical — export the wallet to self-custody.

security.title: Security & privacy
security.body: GembaPass is secure by construction: the on-chain layer is anonymous and minimal, the privileged surface is a single issuer key, and all personal data stays off-chain where it can be deleted.

items.label: No PII on-chain
items.value: The chain holds only an address-to-id capability. Identity, movement logs and PINs live in PostgreSQL with per-company row-level security.

items.label: Soulbound passes
items.value: Non-transferable by construction — the only way out of a wallet is an issuer force-burn, so passes can't be shared or sold as tokens.

items.label: Encrypted custody
items.value: Employee private keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and never decrypted on the access path; the issuer key is the only privileged secret.

items.label: GDPR erasure
items.value: Deleting an employee revokes (burns) the pass on-chain and deletes their identity and logs off-chain.

items.label: Verified contract
items.value: GembaAccessPass follows the GembaBlockchain security standards and is verified on GembaScan.

about.title: Not a typical software house
about.p1: GEMBA IT is the technology division of GEMBA EOOD — a company built on the rare foundation of combined industrial and digital expertise.
about.p2: Our roots are in both server rooms and reactor vessels. This dual perspective shapes everything we build — from the reliability standards we set (because in a refinery, downtime isn't an option) to the practical, no-nonsense approach we take to every project.
about.p3: Founded in 2026, GEMBA IT brings together over 20 years of self-taught IT experience spanning DevOps, full-stack development, blockchain technology, and payment system architecture.
about.p4: We are expanding our fintech capabilities with new payment processor partnerships and banking-as-a-service integrations, enabling our clients to access multi-currency accounts and digital and physical card solutions.
about.p5: Our infrastructure runs on dedicated Hetzner servers in Germany with failover and database replication — because we practice what we preach about uptime and reliability.

privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how GEMBA EOOD ("GEMBA IT", "we", "us") collects, uses and protects personal data when you visit gembait.com or engage our services. We operate from Varna, Bulgaria, and comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body: GEMBA EOOD is a Bulgarian company (EIK 208656371) registered in Varna, Bulgaria. GEMBA IT is our technology division. For any privacy-related request, contact us at contacts@gembait.com.

sections.heading: What data we collect
sections.body: We only collect what we need to answer you or deliver the service you asked for. That includes: contact details you submit through our forms (name, email, subject, message); data required to fulfil a contract if you become a client; standard server logs for security and abuse prevention (IP address, user agent, timestamps); and Cloudflare Turnstile challenge tokens used to block automated abuse. We do not run third-party advertising cookies or behavioural trackers.

sections.heading: How we use your data
sections.body: We use the data to respond to your inquiries, deliver the services you contracted, maintain the security and integrity of our infrastructure, and meet legal and accounting obligations. The legal bases under GDPR are: your consent (when you submit a form), performance of a contract (for active engagements), legitimate interests (security and abuse prevention), and legal obligations (tax and accounting records).

sections.heading: Data sharing
sections.body: We do not sell personal data. We share data only with processors we need to operate the service: Cloudflare (DNS, Turnstile, edge protection), Hetzner (hosting in Germany), and email providers for transactional delivery. For client engagements, we may share data with payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) or blockchain networks strictly as required to execute the transaction you initiated.

sections.heading: Retention
sections.body: Contact-form messages are kept for up to 24 months unless a contractual relationship extends that period. Server logs are kept for up to 90 days. Accounting records are kept for the period required by Bulgarian law. Once a retention period ends, we delete or anonymise the data.

sections.heading: Your rights (GDPR)
sections.body: You have the right to access, correct, erase, restrict or port your personal data, and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interests. You can withdraw consent at any time. To exercise any of these rights, email contacts@gembait.com and we will respond within 30 days. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Bulgarian Commission for Personal Data Protection (CPDP).

sections.heading: International transfers
sections.body: Our infrastructure is hosted in the European Union (Hetzner, Germany). Some processors (e.g. Cloudflare) may process data outside the EU under standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission. We only use processors that provide GDPR-equivalent guarantees.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body: gembait.com uses only functional cookies required to remember your language preference and to run Cloudflare Turnstile. We do not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your browser stores the selected interface language locally; no identifier is transmitted back to us.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: For any privacy question or request, email contacts@gembait.com. We aim to reply within a few business days.
